title: Vertical Cartier divisors of a smooth connected group over a normal base
statement: Let $S$ be a normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Let $p:G\to S$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite presentation [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with identity $e$. The addition, inverse and identity are $S$-morphisms satisfying the commutative group identities; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Assume the geometric fibres of $p$ are connected. Let $U\subseteq S$ be a dense open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion], and put $G_U=G\times_SU$. Then $G$ is normal and integral, and $G_U$ is dense in $G$. A Cartier divisor on an integral scheme means local nonzero rational functions modulo regular units, with the ratios on overlaps regular units. Its support is the locus where these local functions are not regular units. Every Cartier divisor $D$ on $G$ supported in $G\setminus G_U$ has a well-defined pullback $e^*D$, supported in $S\setminus U$, and satisfies $D=p^*(e^*D)$. In particular $e^*D=0$ implies $D=0$. If $L$ is an invertible module on $G$ and $s$ is a nonzero rational section (a nonzero element of its one-dimensional fibre over the function field), its Cartier divisor is given in a local frame by the rational coefficient of $s$. Such a section is an everywhere invertible regular section if and only if its Cartier divisor is zero.

proof.text: The identity section makes $p$ surjective and $G$ nonempty. Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-connected-generic-geometry-core] to $p$: the normal integral base and geometrically connected fibres give normal integral $G$. By [lem-trf-smooth-connected-fibre-normal-integrality] every fibre $G_t$ is integral and nonempty (nonemptiness also follows from $e(t)$). By [lem-pc-smooth-flat] $p$ is flat and locally of finite presentation. Such a morphism is locally of finite type directly from its finite-presentation affine equations; [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] therefore makes $G$ locally Noetherian. Its local rings are Noetherian since they are localizations of Noetherian affine rings (localizing finite generators of the contraction generates any ideal). As $p$ is surjective and $G,S$ are integral, the generic point of $G$ maps to the generic point of $S$: its image specializes to every point of $S$. Hence $G_U$ contains the generic point of $G$ and is dense.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof: local factorization followed by comparison over an irreducible fibre; applied to local Cartier equations with the given section.

proof.text: Fix $x\in G$ and $t=p(x)$. Set $A=\mathcal O_{S,t}$ and $B=\mathcal O_{G,x}$. The stalk map is flat and local by [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Both are Noetherian domains and $A$ is normal, by step 1 and the assumptions. The fibres of $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ are localizations of the integral fibres of $p$ and are nonempty: the flat local map is faithfully flat, by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat], which gives surjectivity on spectra. Each resulting fibre ring is a localization of a domain. A local equation $f_x\in k(G)^\times$ for $D$ is a unit on the generic fibre of $\operatorname{Spec}B$, since that fibre lies over $U$. Thus $f_x\in B_K^\times$: its regular local representatives, and those of its inverse, agree as fractions and glue on this affine generic fibre. Apply [lem-sfb-local-generic-unit-factorization] to write $f_x=p^*h_x\,u_x$ with $h_x\in k(S)^\times$ and $u_x\in B^\times$. A unit germ and its inverse have regular representatives on a neighbourhood, so $D=\operatorname{div}(p^*h_x)$ on an open neighbourhood $W_x$ of $x$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof: local factorization followed by comparison over an irreducible fibre; applied to local Cartier equations with the given section.

proof.text: Fix $s\in S$ and take the equation $h=h_{e(s)}$ and neighbourhood $W=W_{e(s)}$ from step 2. Put $V=e^{-1}W$, an open neighbourhood of $s$. We claim $D=\operatorname{div}(p^*h)$ throughout $G_V$. For $t\in V$ and $x\in G_t$, choose $h_x,W_x$ as in step 2. The nonempty opens $W\cap G_t$ and $W_x\cap G_t$ intersect since $G_t$ is integral; choose $z$ in their intersection. Near $z$, both $p^*h$ and $p^*h_x$ represent $D$, so $p^*(h_x/h)$ is a regular unit at $z$. The final assertion of [lem-sfb-local-generic-unit-factorization], for $\mathcal O_{S,t}\to\mathcal O_{G,z}$ with the same hypotheses verified in step 2, gives $h_x/h\in\mathcal O_{S,t}^\times$. Pulling this unit to $\mathcal O_{G,x}$ shows that $p^*h$ and $p^*h_x$ have the same Cartier class at $x$. This proves the claim. This comparison uses unit reflection, not the false assertion that an arbitrary rational function on $G$ restricts along $e$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof: local factorization followed by comparison over an irreducible fibre; applied to local Cartier equations with the given section.

proof.text: For each $s$, step 3 gives $V_s$ and $h_s\in k(S)^\times$ such that $D|_{G_{V_s}}=\operatorname{div}(p^*h_s)$. On an overlap $V_s\cap V_{s'}$, the rational function $p^*(h_s/h_{s'})$ is a regular unit on its whole inverse image. Its restriction along $e$ is consequently a regular unit, with rational value $h_s/h_{s'}$. Thus the equations $h_s$ glue to a Cartier divisor $E$ on $S$, and their pullbacks show $D=p^*E$. These very equations define the pullback along $e$: write $h_s=a_s/b_s$ locally with $a_s,b_s$ nonzero regular base functions; their pullbacks along $p$ and then $e$ are again $a_s,b_s$, so no zero rational denominator is introduced. Therefore $e^*D=E$. Over $U$, $D=0$, hence $p^*h_s$ is a unit there and restriction by $e$ makes $h_s$ a unit on $U\cap V_s$. It follows that $E$ is supported in $S\setminus U$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof: local factorization followed by comparison over an irreducible fibre; applied to local Cartier equations with the given section.

proof.text: The established identity is exactly $D=p^*(e^*D)$. If $e^*D=0$, its local equations are units; pulling these units back makes every local equation of $D$ a unit, so $D=0$.

source.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof: local factorization followed by comparison over an irreducible fibre; applied to local Cartier equations with the given section.

proof.text: Choose regular frames $v_i$ for the invertible module $L$, and write the given rational section as $s=f_i v_i$ with $f_i\in k(G)^\times$. On an overlap, changing the frame multiplies $f_i$ by a regular unit, so these functions define its Cartier divisor. This divisor is zero precisely when every $f_i$ is a regular unit. In that case the sections $f_i v_i$ are regular generators and agree on overlaps: their rational values agree and the structure sheaf on an integral scheme injects into its function field. They glue to an everywhere invertible regular section. Conversely the coefficients of any such section in regular frames are units, so its Cartier divisor is zero.

source.place: Tags 0B8Z and 0BE8, rational sections in local frames; the Cartier (rather than Weil) zero-divisor assertion is immediate from the local unit definition in the item.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BD7, lemma-in-image-pullback, proof: retain its local generic-unit factorization and irreducible-fibre comparison; the given section selects and glues the base Cartier equations. Last assertion is the local-frame definition, cf. Tag 0B8Z.

New node: it is the 0BD7 affine paragraph for a flat local map of Noetherian domains A->B with A normal and integral nonempty fibres. Every unit of the generic fibre is a base fraction times a unit of B, the base factor is unique mod A^x, and units reflect. I checked the proof myself. p_iB is prime because B/p_iB is torsion-free and its localization is a domain. B_{p_iB} is a DVR with e=1. The symbolic-power intersections I, I' satisfy II'=(rr') by faithful flatness, so they are invertible and principal since A is local. Unit reflection follows from dB∩A=dA. Small cases: field base, DVR base, the normal non-UFD cone xy=z^2, and B=A[t]/(t^2-pi), which shows the integral-fibre hypothesis is needed. B1-B7 pass (statement only, searches recorded, no SGA). Step 1: geometric-core gives G normal and integral, the lem-trf node gives integral fibres, and smooth gives flat and lft, so G is locally Noetherian. Density: p surjective forces the generic point of G onto the generic point of S. Step 2: the hypotheses of the new node hold at every stalk; nonempty fibres come from flat local implies faithfully flat. f_x lies in B_K^x because D is trivial over U and B_K is the intersection of its localizations.
